After sixteen or seventeen months praying toward Jerusalem in Medina, the Prophet turned to the Ka'bah, others turned mid-prayer, and Allah revealed that earlier prayers were not lost.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at facing the Ka'bah, calling it the Qibla; after sixteen or seventeen months towards Jerusalem the Qibla was changed, and he faced it for compulsory prayers.
While praying Fajr at Quba, people were told the Prophet had been ordered to face the Ka'bah, and turned from Sham towards it.
After praying towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months the Prophet faces the Ka'bah; others turn while bowing; Allah reveals the prayers of those who died before are not lost.
People praying Fajr at Quba hear the Prophet has been ordered to face the Ka'bah and turn to it from Jerusalem; Anas is the last left who prayed towards both.
When the qibla was changed to the Ka'bah, as the Prophet had wished, a man's report turned the worshippers at Quba, and some Ansar, towards it mid-prayer.
